## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
The ns/particle curve is essentially FLAT across N at every death rate, with no knee at either spill point. At q=0.01, cost dips from 8.85 ns/p (N=4000, above the L1d spill at 963) to 8.146 ns/p at N=262000, then drifts back to 8.758 at N=4M — a 7% range. Crossing the L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 produces no rise (8.85→8.197). Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.05 sits at 8.6–9.3 ns/p, q=0.25 at 11.2–11.9 ns/p, all equally flat. The absence of any N-knee confirms the algo is not streaming-limited; small-N overhead amortization is minor.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.35 GB/s at q=0.01, N=262000 — 33% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.25 the peak falls to 4.97 GB/s (N=4000), 20% of ceiling. The algo is compute/overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: achieved bandwidth never rises with N (flat ~8 GB/s, declining to 7.76 at N=4M), the signature of a compute floor rather than a streaming limit. The transition is by death rate, not by N: q≤0.05 holds ~8–9 ns/p, then q=0.25 jumps to ~11 ns/p as the branchy respawn path (walk2, non-Halide-expressible) dominates.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within one particle, not across particles. The math loop loads one particle's components via `ldur q7` (4 floats), rearranges with `ext.16b v17, v7, v16, #0xc` and `mov.s v17[3], v6[0]`, then applies `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` on 4 lanes and `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` on 2 more. A gather appears: `ld1.s {v16}[1], [x10]` inserts one element into lane 1. Stride is `add x9, x9, #0x44` (68 bytes = one particle), confirming per-particle iteration. The respawn/scatter path is entirely scalar: 19 `strb` byte stores, 12 `ldrb` byte loads, 18 `csel`, 9 `fcmp`, heavy branching. These byte-granular accesses cannot stream and explain why bandwidth stalls at 33% of ceiling even at q=0.01.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0.01 (near death-free) the algo sustains only 8.35 GB/s = 33% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling, with no cache-spill knee and flat bandwidth across N. Component-wise `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` on stride-68 per-particle access, combined with 19 `strb` byte-granular scatter stores in the respawn path, prevents streaming. The hypothesis does not hold even in the lowest-churn regime.
